author: hoosier state today
title: Two Purdue alumnae join crew for all-Boilermaker Virgin Galactic spaceflight
text:
Purdue University announced on April 15 the final two members of its five-person crew set to participate in a Virgin Galactic suborbital research flight, scheduled for launch in 2027. Beth Moses, a veteran commercial astronaut and Purdue aeronautics and astronautics alumna, and Florence Stahura, a 1992 graduate from the Department of Chemistry, will join the mission known as Purdue 1.
The flight is significant as it showcases Purdue’s leadership in space education and research. The mission will allow real-time experiments to be conducted by alumni, faculty, and students during their journey into space.
Arvind Raman, John A. Edwardson Dean of the College of Engineering at Purdue University, said: “This pioneering all-Boilermaker team will demonstrate that the essential functions of a land-grant university — learning, discovery and engagement — can, in fact, be carried out in outer space. With this flight, the crew is laying the groundwork for the next giant leap to space, on the moon and perhaps beyond.”
Moses will serve as both an astronaut and researcher on an experiment proposed by Purdue’s Weldon School of Biomedical Engineering. She said: “It feels somewhat surreal and incredibly humbling to be flying again. I am very proud to be a flown professional astronaut, but I’m even more proud to be a Purdue astronaut.” Stahura expressed her excitement about joining the mission: “Being selected for this mission is incredibly exciting. I feel very grateful to have the opportunity to participate as a passenger on this spaceflight expedition and even more honored to be part of such an amazing crew. To contribute to Purdue’s first research mission of this kind is truly special — and I hope it’s just the beginning of many more to come.”
The other members include Steven Collicott (professor), Abigail Mizzi (graduate student), both from Aeronautics and Astronautics; Jason Williamson (alumnus); with experiments focusing on fluid dynamics in zero gravity conditions among others.
Lucy Flesch, Frederick L. Hovde Dean of Science at Purdue University said: “This mission is the result of people working together across disciplines, roles and generations of Boilermakers. It brings together alumni, students and faculty who are contributing their expertise…”
Funding for seats comes from various sources including NASA awards for Collicott’s participation; alumni purchase; philanthropic donations support Mizzi’s seat with half already raised toward her $1 million goal.
Beth Moses will also return later this year as associate professor at Purdue’s School of Aeronautics & Astronautics further strengthening cross-disciplinary innovation efforts related to human space exploration.
